### This is a beta release

This build is for testing only. It is published as a pre-release, so it is not offered to
existing installations through the in-app updater — install it by hand from the assets below.

### Coming from the stable release

This line of betas changes how a computer identifies itself, which renames every host once.
Remove each host on both computers and pair them again with the same pairing password. If you
already installed an earlier beta, nothing further is needed.

### Fixes

- A shared display's port is filled in on any refresh, not only when the display is selected. A
  display added while it was showing another host stayed blank for good, because the reading
  taken then said nothing about this host and nothing ever looked again — including after
  switching the display here, which is when the answer becomes available.
- A port the display's own wiring contradicts is no longer stored. VCP 0x60 reports the input a
  display is showing, not the one the reader occupies, so a host that is off screen reads
  somebody else's port; one host recorded HDMI 1 for a display it reaches over DisplayPort. An
  unset port means "not configured yet"; a wrong one sends a switch to the wrong place.
- A paired host that moved is followed, once it answers at the new address. Addresses change and
  nothing moved the pairing with them. Discovery is asked where the host went, but its answer is
  confirmed over the pairing before it is kept — it caches addresses a host has left, and a host
  with several interfaces is reachable on only some. Whatever holds the old address inherits
  nothing.
- A reset leaves the shared list empty instead of selecting a display straight back into it.
- `pnpm tauri dev` starts on Windows again: the dev server watched cargo's build output, and
  watching a file Windows had locked took the whole run down.

### Known limitations

- Undoing a merge leaves the inputs and notes that merging folded into the display the other
  identity joined.
- Merging and host names only sync between hosts running this version.
- The macOS DMG is ad-hoc signed but not notarized with an Apple Developer ID, so Gatekeeper may
  require manual approval.

### What to test

- With both computers on this version and paired, show the display on each one in turn and
  confirm both ports fill themselves in.
- Move one computer to a different address and confirm the other follows it without being told.
